review.translation: [And from every|0] [living {creature}|1], [from all|2] [flesh|3], [you must bring|6] [two|4] [of each {kind}|5] [into|7] [the ark|8] [to keep {them} alive|9] [with you|10]. [They must be|13] [male|11] [and female|12].

analysis.evidence: וּמִכָּל הָחַי means ‘and from all that lives’. The parallel phrase מִכָּל בָּשָׂר ‘from all flesh’ confirms the collective scope. שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל ‘two of each’ then specifies how many to bring.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ and preposition מִן ‘from’, whose נ assimilates to the following כ.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִכָּל הָחַי, “and from all that lives,” הָחַי stands on its own. The following מִכָּל בָּשָׂר, “from all flesh,” identifies the living creatures from which Noah is to bring two of each into the ark.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute adjective used substantivally and collectively.

analysis.evidence: In מִכָּל בָּשָׂר, ‘from all flesh,’ כָּל takes the collective noun בָּשָׂר as its complement. The phrase names the whole group from which the pairs are taken. The following שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל, ‘two of each,’ specifies how the pairs are selected.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed preposition מִן. Its נ assimilates to the כ, producing the dagesh in מִכָּל.

analysis.evidence: מִכָּל־בָּשָׂר parallels וּמִכָּל־הָחַי, “from every living thing.” The command to bring two of each into the ark, male and female, identifies “all flesh” here as the living creatures to be preserved.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.evidence: In שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל תָּבִיא, שְׁנַיִם gives the number to bring into the ark, and מִכֹּל specifies that the count applies to each kind. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה identifies the two as male and female.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine dual absolute, used substantivally.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל means “two of each.” The phrase distributes the count of two across the kinds of living creatures already mentioned, and זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה specifies a male and a female in each pair.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed partitive מִן. The נ assimilates to כ, marked by dagesh.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל identifies what Noah is to bring, two of each kind, and אֶל הַתֵּבָה identifies their destination, the ark.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperfect, second person masculine singular, used as a directive
analysis.sense: bring someone or something to a destination

analysis.evidence: In תָּבִיא אֶל הַתֵּבָה, Noah is to bring the animals into the ark. לְהַחֲיֹת אִתָּךְ (“to keep them alive with you”) confirms that they are to enter it.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add תֵּבָה under its own consonants תבה. The proposed root תאר and gentilic gloss have no support in this passage.
draft.definition: An enclosed vessel that carries living occupants on water.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:14 describes the ark’s wooden construction, 6:19 identifies the animals to be brought inside, and 7:18 describes the ark floating on the floodwaters.

analysis.evidence: תָּבִיא אֶל הַתֵּבָה directs Noah to bring the animals into the ark. The definite article points back to the wooden vessel he was told to build in Genesis 6:14. לְהַחֲיֹת אִתָּךְ gives the purpose of bringing them aboard, to keep them alive with him.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed definite article הַ־ with doubling of the following ת, followed by a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The vessel in which Noah, his household, and the animals survive the flood.

analysis.evidence: The infinitive gives the purpose of תָּבִיא ‘you shall bring’. Noah is to bring two of each kind into the ark to keep them alive אִתָּךְ ‘with you’. The creatures are the implied object of the verb.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed לְ marking purpose

draft.change: Add Genesis 6:19 beside Genesis 6:18 as evidence for the existing sense of accompaniment.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:19 uses אִתָּךְ of the creatures that Noah is to keep alive with him in the ark.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 6:19, Noah is to bring two of each kind into the ark לְהַחֲיֹת אִתָּךְ, “to keep them alive with you.” The pairs are the creatures to be kept alive. אִתָּךְ identifies Noah as the person in whose company they will live.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in its suffixed form אִתּ־ with a pausal second-person masculine singular pronominal suffix referring to Noah.

analysis.evidence: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה יִהְיוּ means “they shall be male and female.” The pairing with נְקֵבָה identifies זָכָר as the male of the two animals.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Include the animal use alongside the human use under a single sense of נְקֵבָה.
draft.definition: A female, whether human or animal.
draft.evidence: Genesis 6:19 pairs נְקֵבָה with זָכָר for the animals entering the ark. Genesis 1:27 uses the same pair for humankind.

article.summary: נְקֵבָה designates a female. Genesis pairs it with זָכָר, ‘male,’ both for humankind at creation and for the animals entering the ark.

evidence.note: Two of each are to enter the ark. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה specifies one male and one female.
God creates humankind זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה, ‘male and female.’

opposites.note: The male is the other member of the pair.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 6:19 specifies שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל, ‘two of each,’ to be brought into the ark. זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה יִהְיוּ, ‘they shall be male and female,’ identifies one member of each pair as female.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ ‘and’ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The female of an animal pair.

analysis.evidence: The plural subject of יִהְיוּ is the two animals Noah is to bring from each kind. The predicate זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה specifies that each pair shall be male and female.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition
